tasks.title: Live migration simulator
tasks.statement: Move a running machine with 16 GiB of memory to another server in three scenarios: a calm, an active and a very active guest. Tune the allowed downtime, vCPU throttling, compression and the moment of switching to post-copy, and watch how the pre-copy rounds reduce the remainder. The exercise is solved when the goals of all three scenarios are met.
tasks.hint: Migration converges when the guest's write rate is lower than the network throughput; otherwise you need throttling, compression or post-copy.

spec_text./scenarios/0/goal: Pre-copy converged, downtime at most 100 ms
spec_text./scenarios/0/hint: The allowed downtime is the stop threshold: the smaller it is, the more rounds, but the shorter the pause.
spec_text./scenarios/1/goal: Without post-copy: the migration converged, downtime at most 600 ms
spec_text./scenarios/1/hint: The guest writes faster than the network can send, so the remainder does not shrink. You need to throttle the vCPU.
spec_text./scenarios/2/goal: Hybrid: downtime at most 100 ms, total time at most 60 s
spec_text./scenarios/2/hint: Switch to post-copy earlier: each pre-copy round here costs about 13 seconds.
